messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: monitor with one chain only
parts:
Hi!

I want to compare results from the bayes NONMEM method to Stan output. Hence I am trying to feed the output from NONMEM into the monitor function from rstan. For unlucky reasons I have only one chain at the moment and the monitor function from rstan does not like this:

R3.0.2> nmm <- array(nmm, dim=c(nrow(nmm),1,ncol(nmm)))


R3.0.2> res <- monitor(nmm, warmup=sum(nm$ITERATION <= 0))
Error in if (d2 == 0L) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
2: apply(sims_wow, 3, mean)
1: monitor(nmm, warmup = sum(nm$ITERATION <= 0))

Is this a known bug in monitor - and is there a workaround?

Just for the record: The number of warmup and iterations is an even number such that the split thing should work:

R3.0.2> sum(nm$ITERATION > 0)
[1] 2000
R3.0.2> sum(nm$ITERATION <= 0)
[1] 3102
R3.0.2> 

Many thanks for your help... and don't worry I am going to ask for more chains, but I haven't run it by myself and I think monitor should work even with one chain (stan does as well).

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] monitor with one chain only
parts:
It seems to be fine:

> b <- array(rnorm(1000), dim = c(500, 1, 2))
> monitor(b)
Inference for the input samples (1 chains: each with iter=500; warmup=250):

   mean se_mean  sd 2.5%  25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
V1  0.0     0.1 1.0 -1.9 -0.6 0.0 0.7   1.9   250    1
V2  0.1     0.1 1.1 -2.0 -0.6 0.1 0.9   2.1   250    1

For each parameter, n_eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor on split chains (at
convergence, Rhat=1).

Does NONMEM return something weird?  What is NONMEM?

Jiqiang

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] monitor with one chain only
parts:
Hi!

Many thanks for your example. R tricked me in this case by implicit conversions:

## works
oneChain <- array(rnorm((warmup+iter)*2), c(warmup+iter,1,2))
monitor(oneChain, warmup=warmup)


## does not work, because passing data.frames into arrays is not a
## good idea and results in a strange type
df <- data.frame(first=rnorm(warmup+iter), second=rnorm(warmup+iter))
oneChain <- array(df, c(warmup+iter,1,2))
monitor(oneChain, warmup=warmup)


Sorry for the noise and thanks for your simple example.

Ah, and Nonmem is a software to do PK/PD and I am trying to compare it's MCMC output to Stan results.

Best,
Sebastian
